history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration explore how to specify and document the resources for which authority is delegated and subdelegated.
history.administration_response: The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation. The Administration has successfully completed the recommended exploration and has responded in full to the Board’s concern expressed in paragraph 239 in chapter II of A/75/5 (Vol. I): “The Board considers it crucial that, for each authority delegated, the scope of the authority be clearly specified.” The comprehensive exploration undertaken has informed enhancements to the delegation of authority portal that allow a more itemized specification and recording of each subdelegation and the resources covered by the delegation. The detailed scope of delegations in the portal allows for better monitoring and reporting.
history.board_assessment: Given that the revised policy has not been promulgated yet, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration explore how to specify and document the resources for which authority is delegated and subdelegated.
history.administration_response: The Administration would like to request that the Board consider this recommendation be overtaken by events. The Business Transformation and Accountability Division has explored how to specify and document the resources for which authority is delegated and has concluded that linking authorities to resources with detailed master data will be cumbersome and increase the administrative burden, thereby running counter to the goal, identified in General Assembly resolution 72/266 B, of developing a simple system for delegating authority. The Division defines the resources under an entity by including master data in all functional areas in the entity parameter table. For example, the funds centre is used for budget and finance and property management, the master cost centre and the Inspira business unit are used for human resources and the purchasing group is used for procurement. These parameters are used to capture the financial, physical and human resources under an entity, and to monitor the authority exercised over those resources.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes that the Business Transformation and Accountability Division has specified and documented delegated resources by integrating master data into entity parameter tables and that using dedicated parameters for different resource types has enabled effective monitoring of authority. That approach aligns with the simplicity requirement identified in General Assembly resolution 72/266 B, and internal reviews have verified the accuracy of the approach in capturing all resource categories. The Board therefore considers the recommendation to be implemented.
